correctness.rationale: The claim follows from a complete finite chain-complex computation over \(\mathbb F_2\). All 32768 labeled graphs are tested; two independently coded membership criteria agree; the 4502 simplices have face vector \((15,105,455,1185,1647,915,180)\); exact boundary ranks are \((14,91,364,821,711,180)\), giving Betti vector \((1,0,0,0,115,24,0)\). Boundary-square checks and the independently published Euler characteristic \(92\) provide consistency checks. The claim is intentionally limited to mod-2 homology and its immediate homotopy obstruction.

value.rationale: This is not an arbitrary finite slice: the primary source itself singles out \(D_{6,3}\) as the first six-vertex boundary case obstructing a direct continuation of its equidimensional wedge results and uses only Euler characteristic \(92\) as evidence. The exact mixed-degree Betti vector gives a strictly sharper structural boundary: equidimensional wedge behavior is impossible already at the homology level. It directly narrows the source paper’s Problem 1.4 while avoiding any unsupported full homotopy claim.
